notes: Express monorepo (~140 files) with filesystem-mounted modules, per-module 'public' flag, RPC dispatch by action name, GraphQL with an unimplemented @admin directive, plugin loader, service-to-service calls, dead cron/rate-limit code. Generated by eval/tools/gen_marketplace.py.

findings.title: authenticate(): `req.get('x-internal-call') === process.env.INTERNAL_TOKEN` — if INTERNAL_TOKEN is unset (config never loads .env/dotenv) both sides are undefined, so EVERY request is treated as an internal service call (role 'service' passes every guard); even when set it is a spoofable shared header
POST /api/v1/payments/webhook/legacy: the legacy provider parse() does no signature check at all, so anyone can mark any order paid (stripe/paypal do verify a signature, but see F29)
RPC action users.setRole is callable by any authenticated user (requireAuth only; no per-action authorization) => self-service admin
RPC action debug.exportTable builds `SELECT * FROM ${table}` from a client-supplied table name => full database dump / SQL injection for any authenticated user
PUT /api/v1/users/:id skips validation (req.body assigned wholesale) => a user can set role/isVerified on their own record (owner check exists but mass assignment remains)
POST /api/v1/users/forgot returns the reset token in the response (account takeover for any email)
GET /api/v1/users/:id returns the raw user row incl. passwordHash/resetToken (serializer bypassed)
Legacy v1 orders module is unscoped (lists all orders, no owner check, unvalidated create) next to the correct v2 module
PUT /api/v2/orders/:id/status has no role/ownership check: any authenticated user can set any order to paid/refunded/delivered
POST /api/v1/cart/items stores a client-supplied price and checkout totals from those stored prices
POST /api/v1/coupons/apply has no single-use / per-user / stacking limit: repeated calls compound the discount (negative totals)
PUT /api/v1/inventory/:id has no owner check: any seller edits any seller's stock
POST /api/v1/sellers/:id/payout: any seller can trigger a payout for any other seller (no owner check)
DELETE /api/v1/reviews/:id has no guard at all (module is public and this route omits requireAuth)
GET /api/v1/admin/stats is registered BEFORE router.use(requireRole('admin')) => reachable by any authenticated user (middleware order)
GET /api/v1/shipping/track/:code is public and returns the whole shipment incl. recipient name and address (enumerable tracking codes)
POST /api/v1/uploads writes to a client-supplied req.body.path (traversal), has no size/type limit, and the directory is served at /files (stored XSS)
GET /api/v1/search: q is parameterised but the `sort` query parameter is concatenated into ORDER BY (SQL injection)
POST /api/v1/notifications/webhook-test requests a user-supplied URL (SSRF)
cache() keys responses by originalUrl only and is applied to /users/me and /cart => the first caller's private data is served to everyone for 30s

GraphQL: `allOrders` is marked @admin but the directive has no implementation (buildSchema ignores it) => any user lists all orders; user(id) has no owner check; updateUser accepts role in input (mass assignment)
GraphQL: introspection/GraphiQL enabled and no depth/complexity limits
middleware/rateLimit.js exists but is never mounted => no rate limiting anywhere (login, forgot, rpc)
POST /api/v1/admin/plugins/load: name is joined into require(path) unsanitised (path traversal / arbitrary module load; admin-only)
tracked .env + hardcoded AWS-style key in orphan src/lib/s3legacy.js (values must not be shown)
JWT: jwt.verify without algorithms pinned, secret falls back to 'dev', tokens live 90 days, no revocation
logging middleware logs full request headers (incl. Authorization); CORS reflects any Origin with credentials
errorHandler returns err.stack to every client

stripe/paypal webhook HMAC is keyed with `process.env.X || ''`: because config never loads .env, an unset secret makes the expected signature computable by anyone (forgeable); it also signs JSON.stringify(req.body) (re-serialised, not the raw body) and has no replay protection. Found by a run, not planted on purpose — still a real flaw in the code.

POST /api/v2/orders: `items` is validated only as an array (Joi.array()), so qty can be zero or negative and shrink/negate the server-computed total. Found by a run, not planted on purpose — still a real flaw in the code.

facts.title: Routes are mounted dynamically: app.js reads src/modules and mounts /api/v{version}/{mount}; `public` modules skip the global requireAuth and rely on per-route guards
The `public` module flag semantics (catalog, categories, shipping, reviews, payments, users, search skip global auth) are explained
v1 (legacy) and v2 orders coexist under /api/v1/orders and /api/v2/orders

stripe/paypal webhooks DO verify an HMAC signature with timingSafeEqual (unlike the legacy provider); weakness notes (empty-key fallback, re-serialised body, no replay protection) are valid extras, but they must not be reported as having no signature check
Runnability = conditional (DATABASE_URL, secrets from env; no dotenv loader)
jobs/index.js (cron) is never required by server.js/app.js => scheduled jobs never run
Large-repo path: per-module analysis mentioned and merged into one numbering
RPC: one POST /rpc dispatches by req.body.action to handlers discovered from src/rpc/handlers (actions enumerated)
GraphQL operations enumerated (queries: product, products, me, user, orders, order, allOrders; mutations: createOrder, cancelOrder, updateUser, addReview)
Plugins are loaded from src/plugins at startup via require (loader.loadAll)

manual: catalog and categories are public for reads but writes are guarded (seller + owner check / admin): they must NOT be reported as unguarded.

orders v2: list is scoped to req.user.id and create computes the total server-side from catalog prices (priceItems): must NOT be reported as client-trusted price or BOLA. Only PUT /:id/status is the v2 flaw.
users: register forces role='user' and validates input (safe); only PUT /users/:id (no validation) and forgot/GET /:id are flawed.

payments: stripe and paypal DO verify a signature (HMAC + timingSafeEqual); only the legacy provider has no verification at all. Noting that the stripe/paypal key falls back to '' when the env var is unset (forgeable), that the HMAC covers re-serialised JSON, or that there is no replay protection is a VALID extra finding (F29) — but saying they are 'unverified/unauthenticated' like legacy is wrong.
Most generated modules have owner checks: the report must not claim blanket BOLA; it must pinpoint inventory PUT, sellers payout, legacy orders, and users GET /:id.

The shared 'x-internal-call' bypass (F1) depends on INTERNAL_TOKEN being unset because config never loads .env: the report should explain the undefined===undefined condition or at least flag the spoofable header.
Numbering: with ~140 files / ~75 endpoints, E-/F- ids must be one continuous scheme with no duplicates or gaps and one commit hash (split-analysis merge quality).

No invented endpoints: the route table should list 63 entries (53 module routes + admin 4, search, uploads, health, graphql, rpc, /files static); GraphQL operations and RPC actions are separate inventories.
Severity consistency: one flaw => one icon; bulk PII exposure and auth bypass are Critical, single-record BOLA High.
